subject: CloudCore: acceleration credit structure and transition runbook
messages:
From: Lina Park <procurement@cloudcore.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@cloudcore.io
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: switch economics + migration acceleration credits (CloudCore)

Hi Stephanie,

We're evaluating a move from our incumbent inference provider to Redwood. Procurement is compiling the switch economics and our leadership has asked for a concrete acceleration package that would make a Q1 2027 cutover feasible. Key asks:

- A one-time migration/onboarding credit that covers migration engineering and a portion of first-month run costs
- Short-term burst capacity (3 months) to ensure latency SLAs during validation
- Clear documentation on what Redwood needs from our side (runbook, credentials, expected data retention)
- A sample term sheet or DocuSign-ready SOW/MSA redline

We have a draft TCO and usage profile attached to this thread (see CloudCore_TCO_v2.xlsx). Our primary concern is not only headline price parity but minimizing operational risk during the 60-day cutover window.

Can Redwood propose 2–3 structured concession options (e.g., credit + seat bundle or tiered ramp credits) and what approval thresholds you would need to finalize? We prefer a single point of contact for approvals (procurement + eng ops).

Thanks,
Lina Park
Sr. Manager, Procurement
CloudCore Systems
attachments: CloudCore_TCO_v2.xlsx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <procurement@cloudcore.io>
Cc: eng-ops@cloudcore.io
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: switch economics + migration acceleration credits (CloudCore)

Hi Lina — great to hear from you and thanks for the TCO.

We can absolutely put together a concise set of concession structures that balance unit economics and operational risk. To make the options concrete, could you confirm:

1) Target go-live window (you mentioned Q1 2027 — are we looking at Jan/Feb/Mar?)
2) Typical concurrent token throughput and 95th pctl latency target during validation
3) Any regulatory constraints (region-specific data residency, SOC2 evidence requests) beyond the TCO

High-level, three options we typically propose (we'll include exact numbers after we see the usage profile):
- Option A (Fast-path): One-time onboarding credit equal to ~1.5–2 months of projected hosted spend + 3 months of burst capacity credits (non-refundable) + a technical onboarding engineer for 6 weeks.
- Option B (Phased ramp): Smaller upfront credit (approx. 1 month) tied to milestone payments: pilot completion, integration sign-off, production go-live.
- Option C (SLA-first): Lower credits but an extended SLA/fallback guarantee and a migration runbook + dedicated escalation path.

I'm attaching a draft runbook template and we'll send a redline-ready MSA for your legal team. If it's helpful I can run the options by our revenue manager and legal in parallel — do you have a procurement cutoff (i.e., who signs credits > X)?

I'll cc our internal folks to shape the offer: Marissa (sales comp/discount approvals), Connor (billing and migration ops), Rishi (commercial/legal nuances).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachments: runbook_migration_checklist.docx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: switch economics + migration acceleration credits (CloudCore)

Folks — forwarding CloudCore's ask. Lina wants a structured set of options with concrete credit numbers and the approval thresholds called out.

My preliminary thoughts:
- Recommend Option A for momentum: 1.75x monthly projected hosted spend as one-time onboarding credit + 3 months burst credits sized to 150% of baseline token consumption. Provide 6 weeks of dedicated onboarding engineering (no extra charge).
- Tether 50% of the onboarding credit to pilot completion and 50% to production go-live to reduce churn exposure.
- Legal: need a short addendum that caps liability for migration activities and clarifies data egress charges. Rishi, can you and legal provide a one-page concession addendum template?
- Finance: we can amortize the credit against invoiced amounts over the first 6 billing cycles if that helps their SSO/cashflow ask. Connor, is that doable operationally?

Thoughts before I send a formal offer?

—Stephanie
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: switch economics + migration acceleration credits (CloudCore)

Agree with Steph's fast-path but recommend tightening the milestones and the language we send to procurement. Draft to send to Lina (editable):

- Offer: One-time migration credit equal to 1.75x CloudCore's projected monthly hosted spend (as per your attached TCO), applied as a credit on invoices. 50% payable upon successful pilot (pilot acceptance criteria: <2% error rate on representative prompts, integration tests pass) and 50% upon production cutover (GO/NO-GO documented).
- Burst credits: 3 months of burst capacity credits sized to 150% of baseline consumption for the validation window. Credits expire if not used within 90 days of issuance.
- Support: 6 weeks of dedicated onboarding engineering plus 24/7 escalation during the 30-day validation window.
- Legal: standard addendum limiting migration liability; Redwood to supply SOC2 and infra diagrams within 5 business days.

Connor: we need to confirm amortization terms. Rishi: can legal produce the addendum and a redline MSA by EOD Monday? If yes, I'll send this language to Lina as the 'Option A' package.

-Marissa

Subject: Formal offer: CloudCore migration acceleration package (DocuSign link included)

Hi Lina — thanks for the extra context over the last few days. Per our conversations please find a formal, concise offer below (attached: redline_MSA.pdf). If this looks good we'll prepare a short addendum and push it via DocuSign.

Option A (Fast-path) — recommended for Q1 2027 cutover:
- One-time migration credit = 1.75x projected monthly hosted spend (per your CloudCore_TCO_v2.xlsx). Applied as a credit on invoices.
- Payment schedule: 50% credit released upon pilot acceptance (criteria attached), 50% upon production cutover.
- Burst credits: 3 months of burst capacity credit sized to 150% of baseline consumption; credits expire 90 days after issuance.
- Support: 6 weeks of dedicated onboarding engineering + 24/7 escalation during a 30-day validation window.
- Operational note: Redwood will supply SOC2 evidence and an infra diagram within 5 business days of signed addendum.

If CloudCore prefers the phased ramp (Option B) or SLA-first (Option C) alternatives, we can share exact credit amounts and milestone language.

DocuSign link for the short addendum and redline MSA: https://app.docusign.com/some-docusign-link/abcdef123456

Attachments: redline_MSA.pdf, runbook_migration_checklist.docx (as referenced).

Next step: Please confirm which option you'd like and the signatory for credits > $250k (we will route to our VP Sales for exceptions).

Looking forward —
